summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, GERD, and prior Puestow procedure was admitted for persistent abdominal pain following a recent hospitalization, exacerbated by running out of oral Dilaudid. He presented with inability to tolerate oral intake, nausea, and a fall due to pain, though spine imaging showed no fracture. Labs revealed elevated creatinine and anion gap acidosis, both improving with IV fluids. He was managed with NPO status, IV hydration, IV Dilaudid, and Zofran for nausea. His symptoms improved, allowing advancement to a full diet and transition to oral medications. Diarrhea resolved, and GERD was managed with continued omeprazole. He was discharged home with a three-day supply of oral Dilaudid and Zofran, instructions to follow up with his primary care provider for long-term pain management, and consideration of outpatient pain clinic enrollment due to high abuse potential.
